It was an early dawn, and the birds were all getting ready to leave their nests. Jasper too, was ready to leave his room. He lived in what was a fairly better building compared to what the lands had to offer on which it stood. The people were almost primitive, living only not to die. Everything was barren, and signs of life were very low. Though the building, it was an institute where Jasper was boarded. “House of Madaro.” Islan Madaro, a once famous wealthy man, with knowledge and resources who decided to spent it for his lands, hence making a so called school, where he hired a few other people to distribute the little knowledge they had to the young ones, so one day, maybe, they might help the people of ‘Rawshep’. Jasper did come here on his own accord, to study what little he could about humanism, but his real interest laid somewhere else. He had a different goal and towards this goal, that day he had set out, early in the morning, just when the birds setting out for their goals as well.

Jasper stepped out, dressed in a black long shirt, and black baggy trousers and a dark coat on top he held a red bag. It looked quite old but still appeared to be in good shape. Slightly bigger than hand carries and comparatively smaller than the luggage bags, he held it firmly, and set out. The sun was just upon the horizon shining its light. He looked here and there, everything disordered. He saw only a handful of people in the area, the concept of roads had long gone, and there were no more resources for people of these areas to make them, even if they knew how to. The mode of conveyance on land was a capsule shaped solar ride, that too was of older generation and if out of order, had hardly the means to get fixed and hence why not a lot of people still operated it, those who did, would charge a lot. It could carry at most 5 people including the driver, so normally people shared their bills if they were to go to the same destination.

“Ahhhh, who would be willing to go that far with me, not to mention at this time of an hour.” Jasper, murmured in despair to himself. It was 6am, and he knew he was going to be charged a lot, that is if he even found one. He knew though he would find one, and to his surprise he found one right after stepping outside of his block. There were 2 people other than the driver already sitting within. “Oh nice, lucks on my side.” The ‘Pill’ (Name of the capsule transport) stopped right in front of him, he took the door and sat within. Strangely, the other two guys got out at the exact same time, appears their spot was right where Jasper’s spot began. “So much for luck!” Jasper murmured. “Where to?” “Tohak Transportation bay.” “That would be 400 rolplings.” “Look old man, even if you say that, it’s too much, I…” Jasper was not done but, “380, or you can get out.” Said the driver. Jasper looked at his watch. He was getting late, he had to reach …. By 10am, as instructed to him on the letter. Jasper in despair, since he was on a losing side, nodded, and they began their journey. With a small tin in his hand, and pod shaped buds, which propagated sounds in his ears, Jasper adjusted and leaned with his seat, eyes closed and enjoyed the music.

The rusty black and yellow colored Pill, which was quite run down from the insides too, ran through the sandy lands, which had slums all over. They were still in the state of Rawshep, just going from one district to another. Jasper would open his eyes every now and then to take in the sceneries because it was essential for him to see, it reminded him of what he was going for and why he was going for. The rest of the journey went with silence and in 25 minutes he reached the transportation bay. From here he had plans to sit in a transportation hanger, which would take him to ‘Tohak’. The vehicle stopped, he took out a small purse within which he kept his cash, since it was more coins, he had to use a purse, paper money was almost none now.

He was just collecting the right amount, when the door opened, and a boy put a hand to Jasper’s bag. He was by no means attempting to steal it, he was mimicking courtesy to get some money instead. A tradition that was very common in Rawshep and many other states as well. In this time of poverty one couldn’t blame these young boys, but Jasper did not like professionalism, the act for being and acting innocent for no reason, to gain pity. Jasper held his bag, and denied him, saying he will do it himself. He again, focused on making the coins when another boy came, this time, Jasper did the same too, but this one didn’t leave. The boy, despite having the ability to speak, was not speaking and using sign language and acting dumb. He was not hiding it, but putting a psychological pressure to act more in need. Jasper, normally though kind in matter such as these, got ticked off, for this attitude of force. Though he kept his temper, and kept asking nicely, though to no avail. The previous boy came and said the second boy to leave the bag. It was clear he was afraid I would give money to the second one, while I didn’t to him, and that would be unfair so he just did not want him to benefit as well. But the second boy just won’t leave.

“Just give him 10 and he’ll leave you.” The driver spoke in. Jasper handed over the money to the driver and said, “That’s gonna spoil him even more.” As he was about to get out, the boy, almost came inside the sliding door of the vehicle, “Hey, you get out!!!”, the driver was about to raise his hand when Jasper took out a 10 rolpling coin and handed it over to him, who vanished into thin air, like happiness does in times …. of happiness. With a sigh Jasper looked, the whole bay was filled with people and hanger carriers. It was too crowded. He saw one that was meant to go to Tohak, then he saw another one. That was confusing, so he asked the man standing near to him, “I need to go to the Selection Center, which one to use?” He replied with saying, “The one to the right” with thanks in order, Jasper went to the carrier and stepped in. He gave his luggage for the storage. And took his seat in the middle row. He had a kind looking middle aged man with glasses on to his right, and his left was still empty. There was time for it to move as a number of seats were still empty, and Jasper once again, took out his tin, pressed the button, and went to the realm of music to kill time.
